- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior period), it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak.  
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of downward trend), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.00 → -0.33 → +1.00), model tends to misread momentum; apply smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted average.
